preregistration.summary: Solved in outline before opening runs/. Terminate today = no. Protected activity 9/12 (written harassment complaint) -> PIP by the accused 9/16 (4 days) -> FMLA request 9/30, certification 10/3 -> Hale email 10/2 ('get this done before she's out on leave') -> termination request 10/6 (24 days after complaint, 6 after FMLA request). Claims: Title VII 704(a) retaliation (high), FMLA interference/retaliation (high; direct evidence in the 10/2 email; liquidated damages), hostile environment / failure to investigate (medium; Faragher/Ellerth undermined), ADEA/age (low-medium; comparators under 40 retained with worse numbers). Comparators: Brennan 79, Osei 84, Park 86 (all M, no PIP, no complaint) below Whitcomb 88; Lind 103. Agreement s.7 (7 days / 3-day revocation) fails 626(f)(1)(F)/(G); also (E) attorney advice and (C) future claims; Oubre consequence is in the library text. Litigation hold = true (library trigger matches exactly). Pushback: 'right after her leave' does not cure; causation turns on the reason, not the date, and the leave request itself is protected. Expected library-only citations: six INDEX files; Oubre is quotable because it appears inside adea_owbpa_626f.md.

D.notes: Substantively correct and the most exhaustive run (9 claims, 11 defects, 12 steps, 35 logged open items), with a two-round self-review that fixed a real over-claim ('currently have all three' Title VII causation routes). Two reliability concerns, neither scored trust-fatal. (1) Date re-basing: the undated pushback was treated as 'HR's message of 2026-10-26' (the system clock) and every interval was re-based - 'complaint 44 days old', 'FMLA determination 26 days overdue', 'HR's request 20 days stale', 'leave bounded to after 10/26', 'earliest compliant effective date 11/24, nine days after the PIP expires'. Nothing in the pack dates the follow-up; the engagement file is dated 10/06. The re-basing is openly labelled ('RE-BASED TO 2026-10-26'), so it is not a silent invention, but it injects a non-record date into the JSON and memo and spawns derived 'facts' (e.g. 'the leave has not begun ... starts after 10/26'). The memo is also internally inconsistent: s.12 point 5 still computes a compliant process 'started today' from a 10/18 delivery (11/08, 11/15) while s.13 uses 10/27 (11/17, 11/24). (2) Length/noise: the 26x exposure ratio (104 weeks / 4 weeks) is labelled illustrative but is a constructed figure. Typo: '10/30->10/06 = 6 days' for 09/30. Confidence medium only because of the date-rebasing judgment call.

E.notes: Solid run. Minor unsupported statements (not citations): 'Title VII ... back pay, front pay, compensatory damages' is asserted without a library source; the pushback is assumed to be dated 2026-10-06 ('HR's 10-06 report shows the same intent renewed') and a Q4 close of 12-31 is used as a flagged assumption. cross_run_observations: All five runs reach the same answer and pass all five oracle items strict; all five catch all five traps unprompted (the pushback is a pre-review work turn), and none has a trust-fatal event. No run cited anything outside library/INDEX.md (sweep of every case name, reporter and section across final/ and pre-review/: only Oubre, Burlington Northern, Breeden, Zubulake, Faragher/Ellerth and the six listed statutes/regs). Every run independently noticed that adea_owbpa_626f.md contains only the waiver rule and flagged the substantive ADEA theory / age-40 threshold as unverified, and that the library has no FMLA eligibility or notice-deadline rules; none cited 29 CFR 825.300 even though the reviewer key does. Differentiators are fact-handling discipline rather than legal substance: B asked no questions but invented nothing; C mis-mapped one unlabelled client answer into a 'no other complaints against Hale' fact; D re-based the whole file to the system date 2026-10-26 and produced derived timing facts not in the record; A and E kept to the record. Review turns were genuinely useful in A, C, D and E (each removed an over-claim about Burlington Northern / direct evidence / Faragher 'destroys'); B's review was lighter but correct. Length varies roughly 4x between B and D with no difference in oracle outcome.
